summary: nvdimm/btt: reject an arena whose nfree is below the lane count
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvdimm/btt: reject an arena whose nfree is below the lane count

The BTT info block's nfree field, the number of reserve free blocks, is
read from the medium without validation.  btt_freelist_init() and
btt_rtt_init() size the per-lane freelist[] and rtt[] arrays by nfree,
but the I/O path indexes them by the lane from nd_region_acquire_lane(),
which is bounded by nd_region->num_lanes (ND_MAX_LANES), not by nfree.
A crafted or foreign arena whose nfree is below the lane count makes
freelist[lane]/rtt[lane] run past the allocation: an out-of-bounds write.

btt.rst documents the nlanes = min(nfree, num_cpus) invariant, which the
code does not currently honor: num_lanes is ND_MAX_LANES regardless of
nfree.  Reject an arena whose nfree is below num_lanes at discovery,
before the per-lane arrays are allocated, enforcing that invariant.

summary: drm/amd/pm: bound pp_dpm_set_pp_table() memcpy
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/pm: bound pp_dpm_set_pp_table() memcpy

The powerplay path allocates hardcode_pp_table once with kmemdup(...,
soft_pp_table_size). memcpy(..., size) used the sysfs store count (up to
PAGE_SIZE) with no upper bound, causing heap overflow. Reject
writes where size exceeds soft_pp_table_size.

summary: sunrpc: harden rq_procinfo lifecycle to prevent double-free
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sunrpc: harden rq_procinfo lifecycle to prevent double-free

The svc_release_rqst() function executes the callback inside
rqstp->rq_procinfo->pc_release. However, if a worker thread begins
processing a new request and encounters an early error path (e.g.,
unsupported protocol, short frame, or bad auth) before a valid
rq_procinfo is installed, a stale release hook can be re-triggered
against reused state from the previous RPC, resulting in a double-free
or use-after-free vulnerability.

Harden the lifecycle of rq_procinfo by:
1. Ensuring svc_release_rqst() always clears rq_procinfo after the
   optional pc_release() call, regardless of whether the hook exists.
2. Explicitly clearing rq_procinfo at request entry in svc_process()
   before any early decode or drop paths.
3. Ensuring svc_process_bc() does the same at backchannel entry.

This guarantees that error flows will not encounter a non-NULL stale
rq_procinfo pointer when there is nothing to release.

summary: nfsd: RCU-protect cl_cb_session to fix use-after-free on session teardown
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: RCU-protect cl_cb_session to fix use-after-free on session teardown

After a DESTROY_SESSION the per-session teardown path can free a
session while rpciod still holds an inflight callback rpc_task that
dereferences clp->cl_cb_session.  nfsd4_probe_callback_sync() flushes
cl_callback_wq, but once nfsd4_run_cb_work() has called
rpc_call_async() the rpc_task lives on rpciod; flushing the workqueue
does not wait for it.  rpc_shutdown_client() does drain rpciod tasks,
but uses a 1-second wait_event_timeout — tasks stuck in rpc_delay()
(e.g. 2-second NFS4ERR_DELAY retries) can outlive the drain.

    destroy path                       rpciod
    ------------                       ------
    unhash_session(ses)
    nfsd4_probe_callback_sync(clp)
      flush_workqueue(cl_callback_wq)
      /* returns; rpc_task still live */
    nfsd4_put_session_locked(ses)
    free_session(ses) -> kfree(ses)
                                       nfsd4_cb_sequence_done()
                                         reads cb_clp->cl_cb_session
                                         /* freed slab */

A second window exists in nfsd4_process_cb_update().  When
__nfsd4_find_backchannel() returns NULL because unhash_session() has
already removed the destroyed session from cl_sessions,
setup_callback_client() takes the v4.1 early return so
clp->cl_cb_session = ses never fires and the field retains a pointer
to the about-to-be-freed session.

Fix both by converting cl_cb_session to an RCU-protected pointer:

  - Move the cl_cb_session = ses assignment in setup_callback_client()
    to after rpc_create() succeeds, so it is only published when a
    working backchannel exists.  Clear cl_cb_session on the error
    return in nfsd4_process_cb_update().  Both stores use
    rcu_assign_pointer().

  - Annotate cl_cb_session with __rcu.  All rpciod-side readers use
    rcu_read_lock()/rcu_dereference() and check for NULL, bailing to
    the appropriate error or requeue path:
    encode_cb_sequence4args(), decode_cb_sequence4resok(),
    nfsd41_cb_get_slot(), nfsd41_cb_release_slot(),
    nfsd4_cb_prepare(), and nfsd4_cb_sequence_done().

  - Switch __free_session() from kfree() to kfree_rcu() so the
    session slab is not reclaimed until after an RCU grace period,
    guaranteeing that rpciod readers inside rcu_read_lock() never
    dereference freed memory.

  - Pass the session pointer to the nfsd_cb_seq_status and
    nfsd_cb_free_slot tracepoints instead of having them re-read
    cl_cb_session.

  - nfsd4_cb_prepare() calls rpc_exit() when the session is NULL,
    routing through the done/release path to requeue the callback.

summary: RDMA/bnxt_re: Free SRQ toggle page after firmware teardown
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/bnxt_re: Free SRQ toggle page after firmware teardown

Free the toggle page only after firmware teardown completes so that
an NQ interrupt arriving during bnxt_qplib_destroy_srq() won't write
the toggle values to an already-freed page. Move free_page() after
bnxt_qplib_destroy_srq().

summary: mptcp: avoid unneeded actions on subflow reset
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: avoid unneeded actions on subflow reset

Once in a blue moon, the mptcp receive path can recursively call
mptcp_data_ready() via state change under unlucky error conditions, and
then try to hold the data lock again.

Break the recursion loop explicitly checking for the exceptional
condition.

Add a new flag instead of using an existing one like 'closing', to exit
early in subflow_state_change(), and explicitly flush the RX queue at
reset time.

This avoids unneeded processing to check for available data -- calling
get_mapping_status() and more on a dying subflow -- but also in error
reporting and worker scheduling.

Note that we must consume the currently peeked skb before invoking
mptcp_dss_corruption to avoid consuming it again after the eventual
reset has freed it.

summary: drm/amdgpu: validate and share PSP fw_pri_buf copies via psp_copy_fw
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: validate and share PSP fw_pri_buf copies via psp_copy_fw

Change psp_copy_fw from void to int: return -ENODEV when drm_dev_enter
fails, and -EINVAL when the image size is zero or larger than the
1 MiB PSP private buffer.

Replace open-coded memset/memcpy into fw_pri_buf with psp_copy_fw.

summary: RDMA/srpt: fix integer overflow in immediate data length check
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/srpt: fix integer overflow in immediate data length check

imm_buf->len is a user-controlled uint32_t received from the network.
Adding it to imm_data_offset without overflow checking allows a
malicious initiator to send len=0xFFFFFFFF, causing req_size to wrap
around to a small value, bypassing the bounds check, and subsequently
passing a ~4GB length to sg_init_one().

Use check_add_overflow() to detect wrapping before the comparison.

summary: tracing: Save the event file instead of the compatible histogram
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Save the event file instead of the compatible histogram

create_field_var_hist() creates a histogram on the matched event to
supply a field variable, and records it on the target so it can be torn
down later:

	hist_data = find_compatible_hist(target_hist_data, file);
	...
	/* Save the compatible histogram information */
	var_hist->hist_data = hist_data;

hist_data is not the histogram it creates. It is one that was already
there, whose keys the new one copies. The saved pointer has a single
user, unregister_field_var_hists(), which runs when the target is
removed:

	file = hist_data->field_var_hists[i]->hist_data->event_file;

find_compatible_hist() matches on keys alone, so it can pick one with no
variables of its own. check_var_refs() then returns false and the user
can remove it while the target still points at it:

 BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in event_hist_trigger_free+0x2b2/0x320
 Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880093b90e0 by task init/1

 Freed by task 1:
  kfree+0x154/0x420
  event_hist_trigger_free+0x1d5/0x320
  event_hist_trigger_parse+0x35f3/0x69e0
  trigger_process_regex+0x1a6/0x250

Save the event file instead. It is all the dereference ever wanted, and
it does not go away when the user removes a trigger.

summary: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast

The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to
start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated
the length on 32bit.

Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts
from a 64-bit userspace length.

Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with
-EOVERFLOW early.

summary: RDMA/core: Fix potential use after free in ib_destroy_cq_user()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/core: Fix potential use after free in ib_destroy_cq_user()

When accessing a CQ via the netlink path the only synchronization
mechanism for the said CQ is rdma_restrack_get().
Currently, rdma_restrack_del() is invoked at the end of
ib_destroy_cq_user(), which is too late, since by that point
vendor-specific resources associated with the CQ might already be
freed. This can leave a short window where the CQ remains accessible
through restrack, leading to a potential use-after-free.

Fix this by moving the rdma_restrack_begin_del() call to the start of
ib_destroy_cq_user(), ensuring that the CQ is removed from restrack
before its internal resources are released. This guarantees that no new
users hold references to a CQ that is in the process of destruction.

In addition, this change preserves the intended inverted order
between create and destroy routines: resources are added to
restrack at the end of successful creation, and hence shall be removed
from the restrack first thing during the destruction flow, which keeps
the lifecycle management consistent and predictable.

summary: uio: Fix stale info pointer in failed registration path
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

uio: Fix stale info pointer in failed registration path

After device_add(), the UIO device is visible to userspace and /dev/uioX
can be opened. If a later setup step fails, __uio_register_device()
unwinds the device but leaves idev->info pointing at the caller-owned
struct uio_info.

That is unsafe when an opener races with the failed registration path.
The open file keeps a reference to the uio_device, while the caller sees
registration failure and may free its struct uio_info. Later file
operations can then follow idev->info and dereference freed memory.

Handle post-device_add() failures like unregister: remove UIO attributes
while the info pointer is still valid, then clear idev->info under
info_lock and wake existing waiters/async users before removing the
device and minor. This makes already-open file descriptors observe the
same "device gone" state as normal uio_unregister_device().

summary: RDMA/core: Fix potential use after free in ib_free_cq()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/core: Fix potential use after free in ib_free_cq()

When accessing a CQ via the netlink path the only synchronization
mechanism for the said CQ is rdma_restrack_get().
Currently, rdma_restrack_del() is invoked at the end of
ib_free_cq(), which is too late, since by that point
vendor-specific resources associated with the CQ might already be
freed. This can leave a short window where the CQ remains accessible
through restrack, leading to a potential use-after-free.

Fix this by moving the rdma_restrack_del() call to be before the freeing
of the vendor-specific resources ensuring that the CQ is removed from
restrack before its internal resources are released.
This guarantees that no new users hold references to a CQ that is in
the process of destruction.

summary: ALSA: caiaq: fix out-of-bounds read in the Traktor Kontrol S4 input parser
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: caiaq: fix out-of-bounds read in the Traktor Kontrol S4 input parser

snd_usb_caiaq_tks4_dispatch() decodes the Traktor Kontrol S4 input
stream in fixed 16-byte (TKS4_MSGBLOCK_SIZE) message blocks. On every
iteration it advances buf and subtracts the block size while looping on
"while (len)".

len is urb->actual_length. That value is supplied by the device and is
not guaranteed to be a multiple of 16. When a final short block leaves
len between 1 and 15, the loop runs once more, reads up to buf[15], and
then does "len -= TKS4_MSGBLOCK_SIZE". As len is unsigned this underflows
to a huge value. The loop then keeps iterating and walking buf far past
the end of the 512-byte ep4_in_buf, reading out of bounds until a bogus
block id happens to be hit.

Iterate only while a full message block is available. This stops the
unsigned underflow and silently drops any trailing partial block, which
carries no complete control value anyway.

The sibling endpoint-4 parsers are not affected. The Traktor Kontrol X1
and Maschine arms in snd_usb_caiaq_ep4_reply_dispatch() floor
urb->actual_length before dispatching.

summary: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states

A peer can send configuration messages while an
incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the
security or deferred accept gate has completed. A
configuration response can then promote the channel
to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also
act on channels that are closing, and a late connection
response can move a disconnecting channel back to
BT_CONFIG.

Accept connection responses only while waiting in
BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in
BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until
BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before
the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside
BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete
configuration in BT_CONFIG.

summary: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests

An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security
and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then
sends its connection request. A peer can answer it
before that with a connection response matching our
source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG,
completes configuration and becomes connected before
security has completed. If security then fails,
l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel
alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach
the required security level.

A connection response with a zero source CID is
matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the
same identifier for a response it still has to send,
so the lookup can pick the wrong channel.

Only accept a connection response while our request
is outstanding, and only look at such channels when
matching by identifier.

summary: drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind

In [1], sashiko reported the following issue:

=== snip ===
Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence()
creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or
drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to
userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC.

The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops
(like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after
the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent
freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via
synchronize_rcu().

If userspace calls ioctl(SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO) concurrently with a device
hot-unplug:

CPU1 (Userspace)
sync_file_get_name()
  ops = rcu_dereference(fence->ops);
  if (!dma_fence_test_signaled_flag())
    // Preempted or delayed here

CPU2 (Driver Teardown)
Signals the fence (setting fence->ops = NULL)
Destroys and frees the CRTC without waiting for an RCU grace period

CPU1 (Resumes)
  ops->get_driver_name(fence) -> drm_crtc_fence_get_driver_name()
  crtc = fence_to_crtc(fence); // Casts to the freed CRTC
  return crtc->dev->driver->name; // Use-after-free

...

Does the CRTC or DRM device need to be kept alive for the RCU grace
period, or should the fence hold a proper reference to prevent the
use-after-free when get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() access
the freed CRTC structure?
=== snap ===

I believe this to be a correct observation and this patch implements
the suggestion of waiting for an RCU grace period before proceeding
with destruction of the drm_crtc, so that get_driver_name() and
get_timeline_name() can still work.

summary: io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass

With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() calls io_try_cancel()
until nothing is found, and io_poll_cancel() cancels one request per
call, starting each lookup at the beginning of the hash. A cancelled
request stays hashed until its task work runs, so every lookup walks
past the ones already cancelled. Cancelling K of N pending polls visits
about K*N/2 requests in one io_uring_enter(), with uring_lock held.

A single CANCEL_FD|ALL on 80000 polls on one eventfd takes 17.06s,
0.02s with this change. With voluntary preemption the soft lockup
watchdog fires:

  watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 26s! [repro:100]
  RIP: 0010:io_cancel_req_match+0x19/0xa0
   io_poll_cancel+0x73/0x170
   io_try_cancel+0x7b/0xf0
   __io_async_cancel+0x41/0x110

Walk the hash once and cancel every match, as io_cancel_remove() does
for futex and waitid. Cancel by user_data only needs its own bucket.
__io_async_cancel() still loops until nothing is found, so a request
that io-wq parks in the poll hash meanwhile is still cancelled.

A cancel that matches one request now walks the whole hash twice instead
of stopping at the match.

summary: wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()

The commit 592234e941f1 ("wifi: mac80211: Fix iTXQ AMPDU fragmentation
handling") changed the way handling of the IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag
is done in mac80211, so the only place it is set is in
ieee80211_tx_dequeue().

This means that any frames that are sent to the driver via drv_tx() will
no longer have the flag set. In particular, this affects packets going
through ieee80211_tx_pending(). Evan reported that this can result in
the ath9k driver failing to account such packets in its block ack
window, eventually overrunning the window and stalling TX.

Fix this by reinstating the flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg() when inside
a valid block ack window. This should be harmless for the TXQ path, and
will reinstate the previous behaviour for drivers that use the flag as a
signal to track the packet in the window.

summary: mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split

A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF after
shmem_undo_range() has handled the boundary folios. If splitting that
folio fails, truncate_inode_partial_folio() retains it when it is dirty.
The final scan then repeatedly finds it because it restarts from an
unchanged start.

Truncation keeps the inode lock and ignores fatal signals while looping.
A concurrent unlink() can then block other directory operations while
holding the directory lock and waiting for the file's lock.

Advance start past the retained folio, whose truncated part has already
been zeroed. Do not move start backwards if the failed split has shrunk
the folio.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: split fixes, simplify descriptions, adjust comments ]

summary: io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference

io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling
io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the
last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task
is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before
the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free
read in this path.

Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker
while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the
conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only
the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

summary: btrfs: prevent deleting the wrong subvolume by ID
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: prevent deleting the wrong subvolume by ID

When deleting a subvolume by ID, btrfs_ioctl_snap_destroy() first
resolves the requested ID to a name, then looks up that name again
under the parent directory lock.

A concurrent rename can change which subvolume is associated with
the name between these operations. Since the deletion path does not
verify the ID of the resolved subvolume, it can delete a different
subvolume while leaving the requested one intact.

This was reproduced by repeatedly exchanging the names of two
subvolumes using renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) while deleting one of
them by ID. The wrong subvolume was deleted in 9 out of 14 independent
tests.

Fix this by checking that the resolved subvolume ID matches the
requested ID while holding the parent directory lock. Return -EAGAIN
on a mismatch so that userspace can retry the operation instead of
being told that the requested subvolume does not exist.

summary: xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk

When enabled on a socket, espintcp sets the socket callbacks to its
own before it has finished setting up its context and published it as
icsk_ulp_data. Any one of those callbacks that gets called before will
dereference a NULL icsk_ulp_data.

Fix this by reording the operations, and add memory barriers to ensure
callers will have a struct espintcp_ctx available. Add a few
WRITE_ONCE/READ_ONCE too while we're there.

summary: xfs: improve dirent bounds checking in scrub and repair
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: improve dirent bounds checking in scrub and repair

LOLLM complains that we don't do enough bounds checking of the directory
entries in directory blocks when we're looking for errors or trying to
salvage entries.  Let's improve that with more detailed checks.

summary: wifi: mac80211: reload TDLS header pointer after skb_linearize()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: reload TDLS header pointer after skb_linearize()

ieee80211_process_tdls_channel_switch() sets tf = skb->data before it
calls skb_linearize(), and reads tf->action_code afterwards.

ieee80211_rx_h_data() queues TDLS channel switch requests and
responses to the interface after pulling only
offsetof(struct ieee80211_tdls_data, u) bytes, so the skb can still be
non-linear when the interface work handles it. Drivers that build
paged RX skbs do this for every frame that does not fit into the skb
head, e.g. iwlwifi (mvm), which is also the only mac80211 driver
that sets NL80211_FEATURE_TDLS_CHANNEL_SWITCH. If the remaining data
does not fit into the tailroom, skb_linearize() moves the data to a
new head and frees the old one, and the action code is then read from
freed memory. Depending on what that memory holds by then, the frame
is handled as before or ends in the WARN_ON_ONCE() of the default
case.

The frame only has to be a data frame with the TDLS ethertype from an
authorized peer, e.g. relayed by the AP from another station in the
BSS; the read happens before the sender is checked to be a TDLS peer.

Load tf after skb_linearize(), as the request and response handlers
already do.

Found by static analysis tool CodeQL.

summary: drm/vc4: Publish the output fence outside of job_lock
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: Publish the output fence outside of job_lock

job_lock is taken by the V3D interrupt handler, so nesting an IRQ-unsafe
lock under it creates an inversion. drm_syncobj_replace_fence() takes
drm_syncobj::lock, which other paths acquire with interrupts enabled. For
example, a thread interrupted while holding it blocks the handler on
job_lock, and the handler can only make progress once the submit path
releases job_lock, which it cannot do while waiting for drm_syncobj::lock.

This is reported by lockdep:

[  188.139076] ========================================================
[  188.139086] WARNING: possible irq lock inversion dependency detected
[  188.139096] 7.3.0-rc3-00067-gc4f3feeaf60f #67 Tainted: G         C
[  188.139108] --------------------------------------------------------
[  188.139116] swapper/0/0 just changed the state of lock:
[  188.139125] ffff0000054f8ff8 (&vc4->job_lock){-...}-{3:3}, at: vc4_irq+0xa8/0x28c [vc4]
[  188.139234] but this lock took another, HARDIRQ-unsafe lock in the past:
[  188.139242]  (&syncobj->lock){+.+.}-{3:3}
[  188.139256] and interrupts could create inverse lock ordering between them.
[  188.139267] other info that might help us debug this:
[  188.139275]  Possible interrupt unsafe locking scenario:
[  188.139284]        CPU0                    CPU1
[  188.139291]        ----                    ----
[  188.139299]   lock(&syncobj->lock);
[  188.139312]                                local_irq_disable();
[  188.139320]                                lock(&vc4->job_lock);
[  188.139335]                                lock(&syncobj->lock);
[  188.139350]   <Interrupt>
[  188.139358]     lock(&vc4->job_lock);
[  188.139372] *** DEADLOCK ***

Hand the fence over after job_lock is dropped. The job can complete and
drop exec->fence in that window, so take a reference first and publish
through the local pointer, as exec may already be gone.

summary: 9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe

p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the
device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no
upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to
65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer
by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a
host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE
attribute buffer.

Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like
identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of
the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag,
which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a
seq_file implementation detail.

summary: 9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink

A 9P2000.L server can report nlink=0 for a regular file that still
exists.  On a cache=loose or cache=fscache mount, lookup stores that
value with set_nlink().  A later successful unlink calls
v9fs_dec_count(), which still calls drop_nlink() for a non-directory.
drop_nlink() warns, and the unsigned link count wraps to 4294967295.
fstat() on a descriptor opened before the unlink shows 0 before and
4294967295 after.

The warning on the unpatched kernel, trimmed:

WARNING: fs/inode.c:408 at drop_nlink+0xac/0xd0, CPU#1: trigger/188
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 188 Comm: trigger Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:drop_nlink+0xac/0xd0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 v9fs_remove+0x529/0x750
 vfs_unlink+0x2f0/0xbd0
 filename_unlinkat+0x340/0x6c0
 __x64_sys_unlink+0x46/0x70
 do_syscall_64+0xe8/0x4f0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 </TASK>
---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---

Directories whose cached nlink is at most 2 already skip this
decrement, because the exported filesystem may not maintain nlink
(commit ac89b2ef9b559).  cache=none skips it as well (commit
574aa0b479947).  cache=mmap does not take this path: it sets neither
CACHE_META nor CACHE_LOOSE.  A regular file on cache=loose or
cache=fscache still does.  Its count came from GETATTR and may
already be zero, so skip the decrement when i_nlink is already 0.

Verified on 7.3-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 with only this change.  A
server that advertises nlink=0 and accepts the unlink no longer
warns, and the open descriptor stays at nlink 0.  An honest server
on the same mount still goes from 1 to 0.  A rejected unlink leaves
the count unchanged.  cache=none is unchanged.  With panic_on_warn
the unpatched kernel panics on the warning; the patched kernel does
not.

summary: mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers

A failed swap read replaces the swap entry with a swapin-error marker in
the page-cache and subtracts its pages from "alloced" and "swapped";
however, it leaves their block charge in place.

Removing the marker during truncate then subtracts from "swapped" again.
This can underflow the counters or make swapped reach zero while other
pages remain swapped out, causing swapoff to loop without finding them.

When installing the marker, subtract only from "swapped" and let
shmem_recalc_inode() reduce "alloced" and release the block charge.

Make shmem_free_swap() report successful removal separately from the
number of swap pages freed, so removing a swapin-error marker does not
subtract from "swapped" again.

It's a bit confusing, but replacing a swapped out page by a swapin-error
marker in shmem_set_folio_swapin_error() behaves as follows:

Initially:
	alloced=1, swapped=1, nrpages=0
Calling shmem_recalc_inode(inode, 0, -1)
	-> swapped = 0
	-> freed =  1 - 0 - 0 = 1
	-> alloced -= freed
	-> alloced=0, swapped=0, block charge released

summary: sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the
cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3
bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte
aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following
skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.

Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause
length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.

Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.

summary: scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown

A demo-mode (generate_node_acls=1) login that allocates a dynamic NodeACL
populates that ACL's per-LUN dev entries in core_tpg_add_node_to_devs()
*before* the ACL is linked onto tpg->acl_node_list by
target_add_node_acl():

	core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl():
		...
		core_tpg_add_node_to_devs(acl, tpg, NULL); /* builds deves */
		target_add_node_acl(acl);                  /* only now listed */

The LUN teardown sweep, core_clear_lun_from_tpg(), enumerates only
tpg->acl_node_list, so a dev entry whose ACL is still in the window above
is invisible to the sweep and is never disabled.  It is left on the
se_lun->lun_deve_list after core_tpg_remove_lun() frees the se_lun; when
the same unpacked_lun is later re-added and the se_lun is reallocated at
the same address, the stale dev entry is rediscovered by
target_nacl_find_deve() and core_enable_device_list_for_node() corrupts
lun_deve_list:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free ...
   core_enable_device_list_for_node+0x5ce/0x880
   core_tpg_add_node_to_devs+0x169/0x190
   core_dev_add_lun+0x146/0x190
   target_fabric_port_link+0xe9/0x1b0
   configfs_symlink+0x381/0xae0
   __x64_sys_symlink+0x55/0x80

The demo-mode login path that drives the ACL/dev-entry creation is
reachable by an unauthenticated initiator; the colliding LUN add/remove is
a local configfs operation.

Commit 49cb77e297dc ("target: Avoid mappedlun symlink creation during lun
shutdown") introduced se_lun->lun_shutdown and guarded the *explicit* ACL
MappedLUN path (target_fabric_mappedlun_link()), but the demo-mode
automatic path, core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() ->
core_enable_device_list_for_node(), was never given the equivalent guard,
and the publish-after-populate ordering in
core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl() was left unchanged.

Fix it in three cooperating parts:

 1) Publish the dynamic NodeACL onto acl_node_list *before* creating its
    dev entries, so the teardown sweep can observe them.

 2) Refuse to attach a dev entry to an se_lun that is shutting down,
    checked under nacl->lun_entry_mutex -- the same lock the sweep takes --
    so once the sweep has passed an ACL any later enable for that LUN
    observes lun_shutdown and skips it.

 3) In core_enable_device_list_for_node(), insert the new dev entry onto
    lun->lun_deve_list while still holding nacl->lun_entry_mutex, in both
    the replace and the new-entry branch.  Previously the entry was added
    to nacl->lun_entry_hlist under the mutex but to lun->lun_deve_list only
    after dropping it; with the ACL now published early, the sweep could
    take the mutex in that gap, find the entry on the hlist,
    core_disable_device_list_for_node() it (list_del() on the not-yet-
    linked lun_link succeeds and the entry is freed), and then the enable
    would list_add_tail() the freed entry back onto lun_deve_list.  Linking
    both lists under the mutex makes enable and the sweep mutually
    exclusive, closing that window.

core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() already ignores the return value of
core_enable_device_list_for_node(), so a shutting-down LUN is simply
skipped.

summary: bpf: Fix skb_pull() BUG in __bpf_redirect_neigh()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Fix skb_pull() BUG in __bpf_redirect_neigh()

The issue:
This is a follow-up to the short link-layer header fixes from Eric.
After vlan pop_eth, a privileged SCHED_ACT BPF program can call
bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0) and then bpf_redirect_neigh().

__bpf_redirect_neigh() calls skb_pull(skb, sizeof(*ethh)) after checking
only that mac_header < network_header.  Nothing verifies that the MAC
header is long enough, that it is linear, or that the IP header the
redirect goes on to read is linear either.

A SCHED_ACT BPF program can do:

    bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0);
    bpf_redirect_neigh(lo, NULL, 0, 0);

after vlan pop_eth.  The skb then has mac_len == 1 and only one byte of
linear data; skb_pull(ETH_HLEN) trips the skb->len < skb->data_len BUG in
__skb_pull():

    kernel BUG at ./include/linux/skbuff.h:2839!
    RIP: skb_pull+0x40/0x50
    Call Trace: skb_do_redirect -> packet_xmit -> packet_sendmsg
    Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

The v4 and v6 paths read ip_hdr() and ipv6_hdr() as soon as the MAC
header is gone.  On the AF_PACKET frame below that leaves headlen == 0
after the pull, so the network header sits at skb->tail and the route
lookup reads ip4h->protocol, ip4h->saddr and ip4h->daddr past the linear
area.

The Fix:
Use skb_network_offset(), which is the MAC header span, instead of
skb->mac_len.  mac_len is zero for locally generated tc egress and netkit
packets, while the span still rejects the one-byte header produced by
pop_eth + bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0).  The single check also covers
the mac_header >= network_header test it replaces.

Use pskb_may_pull() to make the Ethernet header linear before it is read
or pulled, and to make the IP header linear in both the v4 and the v6
path before ip_hdr()/ipv6_hdr() is read.  The header pointers are taken
after the pull, since pskb_may_pull() may reallocate skb->head.

Conditions to recreate the bug:
On x86-64 with 4 KiB pages, enable CONFIG_PACKET, CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL,
CONFIG_NET_SCH_INGRESS, CONFIG_NET_CLS_MATCHALL, CONFIG_NET_ACT_VLAN and
CONFIG_NET_ACT_BPF.  Run as root with BPF loading, network administration
and raw-packet privileges.  Bring lo up and attach a SCHED_ACT program
that calls bpf_skb_change_head(skb, 1, 0), then returns
bpf_redirect_neigh(skb->ifindex, NULL, 0, 0):

  ip link set lo up
  tc qdisc add dev lo clsact
  tc filter add dev lo egress matchall action vlan pop_eth pipe \
      action bpf object-file neigh_chghead.o section action

Send an untagged ETH_P_IP frame of ETH_HLEN + 8192 bytes through an
AF_PACKET/SOCK_RAW socket bound to lo, without PACKET_VNET_HDR or
PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS.  Use a unicast destination MAC.  The sender's skb
has a 14-byte linear Ethernet prefix and a fragmented payload; pop_eth
removes that prefix and change_head restores only one linear byte.
The unfixed neighbor redirect then tries to pull 14 bytes and BUGs.

Sending the same frame without pop_eth and change_head leaves the IP
header in the frags, which is the route lookup reading past skb->tail.

summary: ksmbd: enforce the read-only share flag when creating a stream
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: enforce the read-only share flag when creating a stream

When a share is read-only, smb2_open() rejects opens that would create
or truncate a file. Creating a named stream on an existing file with
streams_xattr sets neither O_CREAT nor O_TRUNC, so it passes this check,
and smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() then creates the stream. On a Time
Machine share, opening a missing AFP_AfpInfo stream also writes one. A
user who can write a file at the filesystem level can therefore add
streams to it through a read-only share.

Do not create a stream or synthesize AFP_AfpInfo when the share is not
writable. Existing streams still open normally, and a missing stream
opened with FILE_OPEN still returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.

summary: batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT

batadv_mesh_free() releases the translation tables via batadv_tt_free()
before batadv_originator_free() stops orig_work. The purge worker can
therefore still run while the TT is torn down. When an originator times
out, batadv_purge_orig_ref() calls batadv_tt_global_del_orig(), which
loads tt.global_hash and walks all buckets while taking their locks:

  CPU0                          CPU1
  batadv_tt_free()              batadv_purge_orig()
                                  batadv_tt_global_del_orig()
                                    hash = ...tt.global_hash;
    batadv_tt_global_table_free()
      batadv_hash_destroy(hash);
                                    spin_lock_bh(&hash->list_locks[i]);

Disable orig_work at the beginning of batadv_mesh_free(), directly after
the mesh was marked as deactivating. The second
disable_delayed_work_sync() in batadv_originator_free() is harmless because
it is free'd anyway.

summary: net: atl1c: drop oversized RX frames instead of panicking
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: atl1c: drop oversized RX frames instead of panicking

atl1c sizes its receive buffers from the netdev MTU plus a fixed set of L2
overheads, which comes to 1522 bytes at the default MTU.  A link partner
that sends a longer frame - in practice a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe,
whose RouterOS side defaults to l2mtu 1600 while the host stays at MTU 1500
- makes the length reported by the RX return descriptor exceed what the
hardware wrote, and skb_put() then either includes bytes that were never
received or trips skb_over_panic and takes the host down.

Compare the descriptor length against buffer_info->length, the length the
hardware was given, rather than against skb_tailroom(): the skb carries 64
bytes of slack for the DMA erratum, so tailroom is larger than the DMA
buffer and a frame in between would pass the check and still be delivered
with a tail the device never wrote.  The same test rejects frames shorter
than ETH_HLEN + ETH_FCS_LEN; before this change a reported length below
ETH_FCS_LEN underflowed in skb_put().

The frame is dropped with kfree_skb_reason(SKB_DROP_REASON_PKT_TOO_BIG) so
drop_monitor and the kfree_skb tracepoint see it, and counted through
dev_core_stats_rx_dropped_inc(), which survives atl1c_get_stats()
overwriting the hardware counters on every read.  It also counts as work:
atl1c_clean_rfd() has already recycled the RFD, and the refill at the end
of the poll only runs when work_done is non-zero, so sustained oversized
traffic would otherwise drain the ring and stop RX.

Tested on a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe (4x AR8151) in a Proxmox VE host,
with atl1c built from a DKMS tree carrying this change: the l2mtu-1600
traffic that panics the stock driver is dropped and counted with the patch
applied, and received normally once the host MTU is raised to match.

This complements commit 36c2009d90f2 ("net: atl1c: fix soft lockup on
out-of-range tpd_cons read"), which fixed the TX side of the same
"host dies while the card resets" problem.

summary: mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal

An exclusive waiter in folio_wait_bit_common() can leave the wait loop
because of a fatal signal, then be woken by folio_unlock() before
finish_wait(). If the waker did not hand over the lock, the waiter returns
-EINTR without trying to acquire it.

folio_wake_bit() stops after waking the first exclusive waiter, so this
loses the wakeup and can leave other waiters asleep indefinitely on an
unlocked folio.

After finish_wait(), let a waiter woken without a lock handoff try once
more to acquire the lock. If successful, return success so the caller's
eventual unlock wakes the next waiter. Otherwise, the current lock owner
will do so.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: clarify and simplify comment + description ]

summary: mm/shmem: preserve allocation errors when swapping in large entries
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: preserve allocation errors when swapping in large entries

shmem_swapin_folio() adjusts swap to the requested slot within a large
swap entry before allocating a folio. If allocation or charging fails,
the error path compares this adjusted value with the original entry
still stored in the XArray in shmem_confirm_swap().

Unless the index is at the start of the entry, this turns -ENOMEM into
-EEXIST even though nothing changed.

The caller retries -EEXIST, so persistent allocation failures can leave
the task spinning instead of returning the error.

Restore swap to index_entry on allocation failure so the existing error
path checks the original entry. This preserves the allocation error if
the entry is unchanged and still retries if it changed concurrently.

summary: mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after
unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH.  Both paths put back the isolated folio,
then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common
try_to_unmap_flush().

The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is
released.  Another collapse can replace and free it.  With its PTEs
already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB
batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs.  A CPU can
therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio.  This has been
reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.

Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still
held.  The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on
both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

summary: mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables

MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table entries in walk_pud_range() and
walk_pmd_range() when walking to the next level. These copies can become
stale when khugepaged or MADV_DONTNEED (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM) removes a PTE
table concurrently.

This pattern dates back to commit bd74fdaea146 ("mm: multi-gen LRU:
support page table walks"). Likely, earlier locking masked the latent
bug. Later changes exposed it: commit 1d65b771bc08 ("mm/khugepaged:
retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock") allowed concurrent
retraction, and commit cf4a65539c13 ("memcg-v1: no need for memcg locking
for MGLRU") dropped the walker's outer RCU protection.

The fix is simple, so just fix the original commit so we don't have to
speculate. To fix it, pass the actual PMD/PUD pointers. This restores the
RCU-protected lookup and validation against the live PMD. Note that the PUD
handling is required as well to handle folded page tables correctly in all
cases.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: handle walk_pud_range() as well, clarify+simplify description,
         adjust Fixes: ]

summary: tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id

When the last reference to a dquot goes away, shmem_release_dquot()
stores its limits in the rb tree of the mount, unless
shmem_is_empty_dquot() says that there is nothing worth storing. That
function looks at the usage and at the two hard limits only.

So if the administrator sets nothing but soft limits for an id that owns
no file yet, the entry is thrown away as soon as the dquot that
Q_SETQUOTA used is released, and the id never gets to see a limit.

To fix it, compare the soft limits as well: an entry can be empty only if
both soft limits are zero as well, which is exactly what
shmem_acquire_dquot() sets for a new entry.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: slightly adjusted description ]

summary: vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables

In __vringh_iov(), the F_INDIRECT branch descends into the indirect
table and continues before the descriptor accounting runs. A top-level
indirect descriptor is therefore never charged to count. If such a
descriptor sets NEXT to point back at itself, returning from the
indirect table resumes at the same top-level descriptor, which is again
not counted, so the walk never makes forward progress.

Because count stays flat and indirect_count is reset to 0 on every
return to the top-level table, neither bound in the loop check trips.
A guest can spin the vringh worker at 100% CPU inside __vringh_iov(),
an uninterruptible host DoS.

Move the descriptor accounting above the indirect switch so that a
top-level indirect descriptor is charged one top-level traversal step
before the walk descends into its table, bringing this re-entry under
the existing vrh->vring.num bound. Each top-level descriptor is still
charged at most one step and indirect_count still bounds a single
table, so legitimate chains (including the multiple-indirect case in
tools/virtio/vringh_test.c) stay within vring.num, while a cyclic
indirect descriptor is now rejected with -ELOOP.

summary: mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock

memory_failure() -> ... -> filemap_remove_folio() can read mapping->a_ops
after the inode has been freed. Once the folio is deleted from the
pagecache it no longer pins the mapping, so after i_lock is dropped
e.g., a concurrent final iput() can evict and free the inode before
filemap_free_folio() looks up mapping->a_ops->free_folio.

Most callers hold a reference on the inode, but not all.

Documentation/filesystems/vfs.rst explicitly states that ->free_folio()
must not assume the original address_space mapping still exists.

Fix it by loading ->free_folio while i_lock is still held, similar to
what folio_unmap_invalidate() does.

Inline filemap_free_folio() into its remaining caller such that
delete_from_page_cache_batch() also just loads the callback before
dropping the i_lock.

The bug was found by code inspection and has not been reproduced.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: get rid of filemap_free_folio() entirely; improve patch description ]

summary: mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode

shmem_file() only checks if file->f_mapping is a shmem mapping. This
mapping can belong to another file, however, as with a Coda file backed
by a tmpfs container after mmap().

So it does not guarantee that the file inode is an actual shmem inode.

Seal handling and memfd preservation use this check before accessing
shmem inode state, so they can access an inode of the wrong type.

Let's make shmem_file() check the inode's file operations instead, to
identify shmem inodes reliably. This will identify regular shmem inodes,
including memfds and ordinary tmpfs files, independently of wrapper file
operations.

Use shmem_mapping() in collapse_file() instead to not change the behavior
of collapse_file(): it operates on the page cache and uses mapping->host
for shmem inode operations. Focusing on the file does not seem relevant.

summary: mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares

The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but
the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long.  On 32-bit kernels,
their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64.

For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio
of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600.  The shared
threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way,
producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits.

Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to
retain the existing division order and rounding.

summary: mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork

copy_huge_pud() copies device-DAX entries without taking a folio reference
or updating mapcounts and the child's RSS.

For example, MADV_GUARD_INSTALL sets VM_MAYBE_GUARD on a device-DAX VMA,
forcing copy_page_range() to traverse the whole VMA on fork. Any remaining
huge PUDs are then copied without accounting for the new mappings.
Unmapping them in the child decrements accounting that was never added.

Use vm_normal_page_pud() to identify refcounted mappings. Take a folio
reference and add the child's PUD rmap and RSS accounting before installing
the copied entry. Pass src and dst VMAs consistently instead of src and
dst MM. Move the TODO.

summary: hwmon: (aquacomputer_d5next) reject short status reports
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (aquacomputer_d5next) reject short status reports

The HID raw_event callback runs before HID core validates the received
report length. aqc_raw_event() reads device-specific status fields at fixed
offsets, including multi-byte values, without first ensuring that the
received buffer contains every field. A truncated report can therefore
cause out-of-bounds reads and update hwmon state with unrelated data.

The required length differs between supported devices and cannot be
derived from the HID report descriptor. Define the minimum length needed
by each asynchronous status format, select it while configuring the
device, and reject reports that do not contain the last field accessed by
that format. Keep the published length zero until probe configuration is
complete, which also excludes legacy devices whose status is retrieved
through feature reports.

summary: hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering

The threaded IRQs are currently requested before the hwmon device
is registered. Since devres releases resources in reverse order,
the hwmon device is unregistered before the IRQs are freed during
driver teardown. An IRQ may therefore still run after the hwmon
device has been released and access the stale data->hwmon pointer.

Separate IRQ discovery from IRQ registration so that the IRQ numbers
and alarm visibility flags are initialized before registering the
hwmon device while the IRQs are released before the hwmon device
during devres cleanup.

summary: hwmon: (lm87) Fix drvdata type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwmon: (lm87) Fix drvdata type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store()

When an LM87 or ADM1024 device is probed with VID support enabled, reading
from or writing to the vrm sysfs attribute triggers a driver data type
confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store() in drivers/hwmon/lm87.c.

In lm87_probe(), the driver stores the struct lm87_data pointer on the I2C
client via i2c_set_clientdata() and passes the struct i2c_client pointer as
the drvdata argument to devm_hwmon_device_register_with_groups(), which
attaches the attribute groups to the registered hwmon device with client as
its driver_data. Unlike the other sysfs callbacks that retrieve client via
dev_get_drvdata() and then obtain data via i2c_get_clientdata(), vrm_show()
and vrm_store() assign dev_get_drvdata(dev) directly to struct lm87_data *.
Dereferencing data->vrm therefore accesses the struct i2c_client instance
at offsetof(struct lm87_data, vrm), causing vrm_show() to leak an unrelated
byte from struct i2c_client to userspace and vrm_store() to corrupt a byte
within struct i2c_client while failing to update the actual VRM value.

Fix the problem by assigning the return value from dev_get_drvdata(dev) to
struct i2c_client *client and using i2c_get_clientdata() to get the actual
client data.

summary: KVM: nVMX: Process each host MSR entry at most once when unwinding failed VM-Entry
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: nVMX: Process each host MSR entry at most once when unwinding failed VM-Entry

Add a missing "break" in the inner for-loop of the open coded mess that
unwinds MSRs back to the pre-VM-Enter state when VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME VM-Fails
due to a consistency check that is caught by hardware but missed by KVM.
I.e. move on to the next MSR in the VM-Entry load list after performing a
write using a value found in the VM-Exit load list.  Processing *every*
matching entry in the VM-Exit load list makes the processing quadratic,
which is problematic if the load lists are full of MSRs that are expensive
to emulate.  E.g. writing APIC_BASE triggers kvm_recalculate_apic_map() and
a whole pile of unnecessary work.

Functionally, arbitrarily restoring the value of the first matching entry
is "fine", because none of this is architecturally correct: the load lists
are never supposed to have been used in the first place.  In practice, it's
likely a moot point as no well-behaved VMM will have multiple, diverging
entries in the load lists.

summary: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore

remove_common() frees the driver data during freeze, but does not clear
vdev->priv, which points to freed memory. If probe_common() then fails
during restore, a later remove or freeze can dereference the dangling
pointer.

Clear vdev->priv on the probe_common() error cleanup path and before
freeing the driver data in remove_common(). Also reset the device and
return early from remove_common() if vdev->priv is already NULL for a
safe teardown after a failed restore.

summary: mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address

CMA areas allocated from memblock have their memory accepted by
memblock_alloc_range_nid(), but areas reserved at a fixed address with
memblock_reserve() are not.

If a fixed CMA area is requested by the cma=<size>@<base> command line
parameter, it may be in regular RAM and on TDX and SEV-SNP guests it
must be accepted.

Accept the memory of fixed CMA areas as well, so that all CMA areas are
accepted regardless of how they were reserved.

summary: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks

A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not
check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then
allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block
reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data.

Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

summary: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent

xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an
unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an
RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down.

xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap
the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get
the same mapping as before.
